meta.name: BA's Best Bolognese
meta.total_time: ~3.5 hrs (1 hr active, 2-2.5 hr passive simmer)
meta.description: Slow-simmered northern Italian meat sauce: beef chuck and pancetta, white wine reduction, milk and stock for richness. 2-2.5 hour low simmer until sloppy-joe texture. Tossed with fresh tagliatelle (or dry rigatoni) and Parmesan.

change_log.summary: Initial recipe imported from Bon Appétit's BA's Best Bolognese (via Paprika app screenshots). Source text preserved in original-recipes.md.

vessels.name: Food Processor
vessels.reuse: Pulse mirepoix once, then put away — not used again.

vessels.name: Small Bowl
vessels.reuse: Holds pulsed mirepoix until added to pot during soften-soffritto.

vessels.name: Dutch Oven (or large heavy pot)
vessels.reuse: Brown beef → wipe out → cook pancetta → soften veg → reduce wine → bloom paste → low simmer 2-2.5 hr. Single vessel for entire sauce.

vessels.name: Medium Bowl
vessels.reuse: Holds browned beef until returned to pot during reduce-wine.

vessels.name: Large Pot
vessels.reuse: Boil pasta water. Reserve 1 cup pasta water with measuring cup before draining.

ingredients.name: Ground Beef Chuck (20% fat), patted dry
Pasta (1 lb fresh tagliatelle/pappardelle OR dry rigatoni)
Parmesan (finely grated; plus more for plating)

states.title: Pulse Mirepoix in Food Processor
states.direction: Pulse onion, celery, and carrot in food processor until very finely chopped. Transfer to small bowl and set aside.
states.exit_condition: Vegetables are uniformly very finely chopped (near-paste consistency, no chunks larger than ~3mm) and transferred to small bowl.

states.title: Brown the Beef in Clumps
states.direction: Heat olive oil in Dutch oven over medium. Break beef into ~4cm (1.5") clumps and add to pot; season lightly with 2g kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally but NOT breaking the meat apart, 6-8 min. Beef may be gray in spots and still pink in center — that's fine. Transfer beef with slotted spoon to medium bowl.
states.exit_condition: Beef clumps are lightly browned on the outside (Maillard color, not crisp), still pink in centers, and transferred to medium bowl. Some fat rendered into pot.

notes.text: Don't break the meat into fine pieces here. Larger 4cm clumps brown better — final fine-grind texture happens later during wine reduction.

reminders.prompt: Note Maillard color before transferring beef

states.title: Crisp the Pancetta
states.direction: Wipe out pot. Add pancetta and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, 6-8 min until pancetta has released some fat and is crisp.
states.exit_condition: Pancetta is crisp and lightly golden, with rendered fat pooled in pot.

states.title: Soften Soffritto
states.direction: Add the pulsed mirepoix to pot with crisp pancetta. Cook, stirring occasionally, 6-8 min until vegetables are very soft and beginning to stick to surface of pot.
states.exit_condition: Vegetables are very soft (no resistance), reduced in volume, and beginning to stick/brown on bottom of pot (this fond builds flavor).

states.title: Return Beef + Reduce Wine
states.direction: Return browned beef (and any juices) to pot. Pour in white wine. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, smashing down on beef with wooden spoon, 12-15 min until wine is fully evaporated, surface of pot is almost dry, and meat is broken into fine 'little bits' texture.
states.exit_condition: Wine is fully evaporated, pot surface is almost dry, beef has been smashed to fine 'little bits' texture (looks finely ground, not in clumps).

notes.text: The smashing here is the whole point — this is when the meat transforms from clumps into the fine, almost-paste texture that defines real Bolognese. Takes effort. Take breaks if your wrist tires.

states.title: Bloom Tomato Paste + Aromatics
states.direction: Add tomato paste, bay leaf, and pinch of grated nutmeg. Cook, stirring occasionally and still pressing down on meat, about 5 min until tomato paste is slightly darkened (rust-colored).
states.exit_condition: Tomato paste has darkened from bright red to rust/brick color and smells sweet-roasted (not sharp/raw).

states.title: Low Simmer 2-2.5 Hours
states.direction: Pour chicken stock and whole milk into pot; add a 1g pinch of kosher salt. Reduce heat to the lowest setting and cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, 2-2.5 hours until meat is very, very tender and sauce has the texture of sloppy joe mixture. There should be NO rapid bubbles — only the occasional small bubble or two. If liquid reduces before meat is tender, add ½ cup (~120g) extra stock and continue. Discard bay leaf. Taste sauce and adjust seasoning with kosher salt (~3g final); keep warm.
states.exit_condition: Meat is very tender, sauce has sloppy-joe texture and look (loose but not soupy, glossy with rendered fat), bay leaf removed, salt adjusted to taste. No rapid bubbles throughout — only occasional small bubbles indicate correct heat.

notes.text: Lowest possible heat is critical. Rapid bubbling = too hot = sauce reduces too fast and burns on bottom. If you see active bubbling, drop heat further or move pot off-center on the burner.
Sauce can be made up to 4 days ahead — cover and chill. Reheat gently before tossing with pasta.

reminders.prompt: Sauce texture at 2hr — sloppy joe yet?

states.title: Cook Pasta in Salted Water
states.direction: Bring large pot of water to rolling boil. Add 30g kosher salt (heavily salted, sea-water salty). Add pasta. For fresh tagliatelle/pappardelle: cook ~3 min. For dry rigatoni: cook until very al dente, ~2 min less than package directions. Reserve 1 cup (~240g) pasta cooking water with liquid measuring cup BEFORE draining.
states.exit_condition: Pasta is very al dente (firmer than final desired texture — will finish in sauce). 1 cup (~240g) starchy pasta water reserved before draining.

notes.text: Reserve pasta water FIRST, drain second. Easy to forget — set the measuring cup beside the pot before adding pasta.

states.title: Toss Pasta + Sauce + Pasta Water
states.direction: Using tongs, transfer pasta directly to pot of sauce. Add reserved 1 cup (~240g) pasta water and 57g grated Parmesan. Increase heat to medium, bring to a simmer, and cook, tossing constantly, 2 min until pasta is al dente and liquid is slightly thickened/glossy.
states.exit_condition: Pasta is fully al dente (final texture), sauce coats every strand glossily (slightly thickened from starch + cheese emulsion), liquid is no longer pooling.

states.title: Plate + Top with Parmesan
states.direction: Transfer pasta to serving platter or individual bowls. Top generously with additional finely grated Parmesan.
states.exit_condition: Pasta plated, extra Parmesan grated over top.

methods.detail: Warm sauce in pot over low heat, stirring occasionally. Add splash of stock or water if reduced too thick. ~10 min.
Add 2 Tbsp water to pan, cover, low heat, stir occasionally to redistribute moisture. ~5 min for one portion.
Cover bowl, 50% power, stir every 60s until heated through. ~3-4 min for one portion. Splash of water helps if dry.
